Everyone knows Germany was split into four occupation zones. Austria was too, and the occupation lasted ten years. Here is the map most people forget.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Soviet troops crossed into Austria on 29 March 1945. American, French and British forces followed on 26 April, 29 April and 8 May. On 27 April Karl Renner's provisional government declared independence from Nazi Germany.

2/ The Soviets held Lower Austria, Burgenland and the Mühlviertel. The US took Salzburg and Upper Austria south of the Danube, Britain East Tyrol, Carinthia and Styria, and France Vorarlberg and North Tyrol. Zones were agreed on 9 July 1945.
3/ Vienna sat inside the Soviet zone but was divided among all four powers too. The historic centre was an international zone, where the occupiers took turns controlling it month by month.
4/ In November 1943 the Allies' Moscow Declaration called Austria 'the first victim of Nazi aggression' and treated the 1938 Anschluss as null and void.
5/ In the Soviet zone, a body called USIA was set up on 27 June 1946. It pulled together over 400 expropriated enterprises and held about 5% of Austrian output.
6/ The State Treaty was signed in Vienna on 15 May 1955 and took effect on 27 July. The last occupation troops left on 25 October, and parliament declared neutrality the next day.
Germany's four zones became two countries. Austria's four zones became one neutral state. Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
